body.html: Who Baanpooya is for — to put it plainly, Baanpooya Hotel and Resort isn't a luxury hotel and isn't trying to be · it's a small 13-room resort in a garden-home style, run hands-on by the owners in a friendly way, tucked into a suburban lane in Wang Hin, Mueang Tak · according to real reviews, the best fit is budget travelers, backpackers, long-haul drivers who need a one-night stopover, and small families who want somewhere quiet and low-key · another group that especially likes it is people traveling with pets, since this is one of the few stays in Tak that clearly says it accepts pets (there's a fee, so ask ahead) · if you're after a hotel with a fancy lobby, a big pool, a gym, or five-star service, this isn't the answer — you'd be better off with a riverside hotel in central Tak by the Ping River · but if your brief is "comfortable, quiet, clean, easy to park, cheap to pay," Baanpooya fits that group well at a price that's hard to find these days · the place is still open, with an active Facebook page and listings on booking platforms like Trip.com and Booking.com.

Location and getting around — Baanpooya sits at 114/1 Moo 9, Old Tak–Kamphaeng Phet Road (Highway 104), Wang Hin, Mueang Tak · the strong point of the location is that it's on the edge of town in a quiet, uncrowded lane, but not far from the center — about 1.5 km from downtown Tak and around 3 km from the Ping River, which is the main tourist area · from Tak bus terminal it's about a 15-minute drive · because it sits right on the Old Tak–Kamphaeng Phet Road, it's a great fit for people driving through Tak heading north, heading south, or turning off to Mae Sot via Highway 12 who just need a one-night stop · the honest caveat is that it's in a suburban lane, not somewhere you can walk to things, so it's fairly inconvenient without your own vehicle, since there aren't restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance like a hotel in the center · real reviews give the location a middling score, praising it as easy to find with clear signs, but stressing that you really need a vehicle to make it work · anyone traveling by car or motorbike has the biggest advantage, since there's a spacious parking lot with plenty of room and no jostling for a spot.

"Booked it for a one-night stop while driving north. Super cheap, but the room was bigger and cleaner than expected · plenty of parking, peaceful and quiet, slept great with no traffic noise — far more than worth the price."

Room types and decor — Baanpooya has only 13 rooms in total, split into three main types per the property's own info · it starts with 5 single rooms and 5 standard double rooms in the starting range of around THB 400 per night · plus 3 VIP rooms that are larger and better appointed, with prices nudging up to around THB 500 per night (rates on booking platforms during peak periods or long weekends can climb into four figures) · the decor is simple, garden-home style, focused on practicality over luxury · the most interesting note from real reviews is the praise that the rooms are spacious, not cramped or crowded, clean, and the beds are comfortable — something many people say went beyond expectations for a price in the hundreds · every room has air conditioning, TV, a small fridge, towels, soap, shampoo, and free drinking water · the bathrooms are private and, according to reviews, roomy, with water heaters that work well · there's one small detail reviews warn about and you should know up front: in some rooms the water-heater switch is outside the bathroom, which leaves some new guests puzzled as to why the water isn't hot — if you turn on the water and it's not warm, look for the switch on the wall outside first · some rooms have no back balcony, while others have a sitting area and a balcony facing the garden, depending on the room type you book.

Facilities and atmosphere — you have to understand first that Baanpooya is a small resort, so the facilities focus on the essentials rather than the extras of a big resort · the most praised point is the quiet, peaceful garden-home atmosphere, with a terrace and a small garden, which makes it feel relaxing, more like staying at a relative's place upcountry than at a hotel · there's plenty of parking on the grounds, a key advantage for drivers, with easy parking and nothing to worry about · there's 24-hour security and free Wi-Fi throughout, which reviews say works well · and as mentioned, the place is pet-friendly, which is what travelers with a dog or cat look for · what it doesn't have, and you should know before booking, is a gym, a spa, or a lift (it's a one-to-two-storey resort-style building) · the pool is a point where info from each platform doesn't quite line up — some sources list a pool, some don't — so it's best to call the property directly or check Facebook to confirm before you go if the pool is a deciding factor, rather than counting on it in advance.

Food and the Baanpooya kitchen — what sets Baanpooya apart from your typical budget stay is the Baanpooya kitchen, an on-site dining room that cooks for guests across breakfast, lunch, and dinner · there's an air-conditioned seating area as well as outdoor seating to take in the garden · on breakfast, real reviews say there's free tea, coffee, bread, and biscuits, and if you want something more substantial you can order extra dishes at modest prices, like rice porridge with toppings for around THB 40, which reviews say tastes fine and is filling · having a kitchen on-site is a real plus for a suburban location like this, since there aren't restaurants within walking distance like in the center, so you don't have to drive out far to find food when you wake up · do note that, since it's a small resort cooking to order, service hours may not run all day like at a big hotel — if you arrive late or want dinner, give them a heads-up or check the kitchen's hours in advance · overall, the food is an extra that makes staying here much more convenient, especially for people without a vehicle or who'd rather not head out in the evening.

Service — because it's a small resort run by the owners and their family, the service here has the friendly, upcountry feel of a small-town stay · most real reviews praise the owners and staff as friendly, easy to talk to, and helpful with whatever comes up · check-in and check-out are fairly informal, with check-in after 2:00 PM and check-out before 12:00 PM as the property states · to be straight about it, since it's a small place without a lot of staff, at times when the owner is away or several guests check in at once, getting hold of someone may take a bit of waiting — it's best to call ahead and arrange a time, especially if you're arriving outside normal hours · there are also a few reviews on international platforms grumbling about certain rules or communication that left them uneasy, which is worth being aware of — since it's a family-run place, the experience can come down to communication and setting expectations on a case-by-case basis more than at a chain hotel with fixed standards.

What real reviews say (the good and the bad) — pulling from Trip.com, Booking.com, Tripadvisor, and Thai review blogs, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: very cheap for what you get, rooms bigger and cleaner than expected, comfortable beds, a quiet, peaceful garden-home atmosphere on the edge of town, spacious parking, Wi-Fi that works well, a kitchen on-site, and pet-friendly · Thai review blogs even rate cleanliness and atmosphere very highly, concluding it's a good fit for backpackers · On the watch-out side: the location is in a suburban lane and is inconvenient without a vehicle since you can't walk anywhere, the water-heater switch in some rooms is outside the bathroom and causes confusion, it's a small place so the basic facilities aren't as complete as a big hotel, the decor is simple rather than modern, and a few reviews on international platforms give middling scores over communication and the property's rules · the overall score reflects the character of the place — Booking.com gives it around 8.1 in the "good value" range, while Tripadvisor, which leans on foreign reviewers, gives a middling score of around 3 out of 5 · read together, you can see that people who come expecting a quiet, budget stay are usually happy, while those expecting a full-service hotel may feel lukewarm.

"Clean, spacious room, lovely and quiet, and the owners are sweet and friendly · the only downside is it's in a lane, so without a vehicle it's a hassle — you can't walk out to find food — but there's a kitchen on-site cooking for you, so it's not a big problem if you plan well."

Price and value — this is Baanpooya's strongest point, no question · single and double rooms start at around THB 400/night and VIP rooms at around THB 500/night at standard rates, while on booking platforms during peak periods a double room can run from around THB 700 up to the low thousands depending on season and holidays · compared with hotels in central Tak that start at around THB 650–900, like White House Hotel or Silayok Grand, Baanpooya is in the cheapest group in town · what makes it good value isn't just the low number, but getting a spacious, clean, quiet room with plenty of parking and a kitchen on-site, which is hard to find at this price · of course you trade that for a location that needs a vehicle and facilities that are basic · but if the brief is a cheap one-night stay or somewhere quiet for genuine rest, every baht you spend feels well returned, and it's why many reviews use the phrase "more than worth the price."

Things to know before booking — a few things help make a stay at Baanpooya go smoothly · one, since it's a small place in a suburban lane, you should have your own car or motorbike for convenience, since there are no restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance · two, if you arrive late or want to use the kitchen, call ahead to arrange a time and check the kitchen's hours at the property's number · three, remember the water-heater switch that may be outside the bathroom so you're not puzzled at shower time · four, if you're bringing a pet, you must give notice and ask about the fee in advance, since there's a pet policy but with conditions · five, children up to age 5 stay free using existing beds, while children up to age 12 are charged around THB 200/night extra, and there are no cots provided · six, since there are only 13 rooms and it's popular with budget travelers, rooms fill up fast during festivals or long weekends, so book or call ahead · seven, it's best to confirm the price and room type directly with the property again, since at a small place the prices and details on booking platforms may not always match what's on the ground.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Baanpooya Hotel and Resort is the best fit for travelers who want a quiet, clean, spacious room at a genuinely low price, with plenty of parking and a garden-home feel on the edge of town · it's good value among the under-THB-1,000 stays in Tak, and works well as a one-night stop while driving north or out to Mae Sot, as well as for people traveling with pets · if you're looking for a hotel in the center where you can walk along the Ping River, with a big pool or full-service amenities, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a riverside hotel by the Ping River in central Tak instead · but for a trip where you're driving yourself and mainly want quiet, cleanliness, and value, Baanpooya delivers, and it's why budget travelers keep coming back and spreading the word.

faq.q: Where in Tak is Baanpooya Hotel and Resort · can you get around on foot?
faq.a: It's at 114/1 Moo 9, Old Tak–Kamphaeng Phet Road (Highway 104), Wang Hin, Mueang Tak, a small resort in a suburban lane · about 1.5 km from downtown Tak and around 3 km from the Ping River · roughly a 15-minute drive from Tak bus terminal · since it's in a lane, you can't walk to restaurants or convenience stores, so a car or motorbike is recommended.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Baanpooya Hotel and Resort · what room types are there?
faq.a: There are 13 rooms in total · single and standard double rooms start at around THB 400/night · VIP rooms run around THB 500/night · on booking platforms during peak periods or long weekends, a double room can climb to around THB 700 and up · every room has air conditioning, TV, a fridge, a private bathroom with a water heater, and free drinking water · it's best to confirm the price with the property directly.

faq.q: Does Baanpooya have food and parking · is it pet-friendly?
faq.a: It has the Baanpooya kitchen, an on-site dining room that cooks breakfast, lunch, and dinner (breakfast has free tea, coffee, and bread, with extra dishes to order, like rice porridge for around THB 40) · there's plenty of free parking · and it's pet-friendly, but with a fee and conditions, so call to give notice and ask in advance.

faq.q: Who is Baanpooya Hotel and Resort for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for budget travelers, backpackers, drivers passing through Tak who need a one-night stop, small families who want somewhere quiet, and people traveling with pets · the selling points are spacious, clean rooms at an easy price, a quiet, peaceful atmosphere, and plenty of parking · if you're looking for a hotel in the center where you can walk along the Ping River or want a big pool, a riverside hotel by the Ping River may suit you better.

faq.q: How does the water heater at Baanpooya work · anything to watch out for?
faq.a: Real reviews warn that the water-heater switch in some rooms is on the wall outside the bathroom, which leaves some new guests puzzled as to why the water isn't hot — if you turn on the water and it's not warm, look for the switch outside first · it's also a small, family-run place, so contacting them or checking in can mean a wait at times; it's best to call ahead to arrange a time, especially if you arrive late.
